output.body:
# M1 Identity: Create and verify ABHA

## In plain words

Milestone 1, Create and verify ABHA: creating an
[ABHA number](abha-number.md), logging a person in, reading and updating
their profile, downloading the ABHA card, and the
[gateway](gateway.md) session and token calls that everything else
depends on. Most of these APIs are mandatory for both private and
government integrators, with Aadhaar demographic authentication the
exception: mandatory for government integrators, not required for
private ones. See [M1](/docs/hiecm/v3/api/m1).

## Before you start

Nothing. A glossary entry assumes no prior reading.

## What happens

Nothing happens here. This entry defines a term, it does not describe a call.

## How you know it worked

You have understood this when you can say whether your system needs M1 without reading the endpoint list.

## When it goes wrong

Building M1 because it is first. A system that never creates or reads an
ABHA does not need it.
output.summary: The milestone covering ABHA creation, login and profile.
output.title: M1 Identity: Create and verify ABHA

output.body:
# M2 Health Information Provider: Create and link records

## In plain words

Milestone 2, sharing records as a [HIP](hip.md): turning your records
into [FHIR](fhir.md) bundles, grouping them into
[care contexts](/docs/hiecm/v3/concepts/care-context), linking those to a patient's
[ABHA address](abha-address.md), answering [discovery](discovery.md), and
encrypting and pushing data when consent allows. See
[M2](/docs/hiecm/v3/api/m2).

## Before you start

Nothing. A glossary entry assumes no prior reading.

## What happens

Nothing happens here. This entry defines a term, it does not describe a call.

## How you know it worked

You have understood this when you can say whether your system holds records that other systems should be able to find.

## When it goes wrong

Assuming M2 alone makes records visible. Nothing you hold is
discoverable until a care context is linked.
output.summary: The milestone covering care context linking, discovery and sending records.
output.title: M2 Health Information Provider: Create and link records

output.body:
# M3 Health Information User: Fetch data with consent

## In plain words

Milestone 3, consent and reading records as an [HIU](hiu.md): raising a
consent request, tracking its status, handling the grant or denial
callback, fetching the [consent artefact](consent-artefact.md),
requesting health information and decrypting what arrives. See
[M3](/docs/hiecm/v3/api/m3).

## Before you start

Nothing. A glossary entry assumes no prior reading.

## What happens

Nothing happens here. This entry defines a term, it does not describe a call.

## How you know it worked

You have understood this when you can say whether your system asks for records it does not hold.

## When it goes wrong

Treating a granted consent as permanent. It carries a date range and a
lifetime, and a patient can revoke it at any point.
output.summary: The milestone covering consent requests and fetching someone else's records.
output.title: M3 Health Information User: Fetch data with consent

output.body:
# M4 Registry Integration: Register facilities and professionals

## In plain words

Milestone 4, the registries: creating an [HPID](hpid.md) on the
[HPR](hpr.md) and onboarding a facility to the [HFR](hfr.md). Also
called NHPR, the National Healthcare Professionals and Facilities
Registry. See [M4](/docs/hiecm/v3/api/m4).

## Before you start

Nothing. A glossary entry assumes no prior reading.

## What happens

Nothing happens here. This entry defines a term, it does not describe a call.

## How you know it worked

You have understood this when you can say whether your system registers professionals or facilities.

## When it goes wrong

Leaving M4 until last. Facility onboarding is reviewed by NHA and can
take days, so a late start blocks go live.
output.summary: The milestone covering professional and facility registration.
output.title: M4 Registry Integration: Register facilities and professionals

reply.Text:
ABDM sandbox milestones are development stages that organize integration features into four sequential phases:

**M1 — Identity**: Create and verify ABHA
- ABHA number creation, login, and profile management
- Gateway session and token calls (the foundation for all other calls)
- Mandatory for most integrators

**M2 — Health Information Provider**: Create and link records
- Convert records into FHIR bundles
- Group records into care contexts
- Link care contexts to a patient's ABHA address
- Answer discovery requests and share data when consent is granted

**M3 — Health Information User**: Fetch data with consent
- Raise consent requests and track their status
- Fetch and decrypt health information from other systems
- Handle consent grants or denials

**M4 — Registry Integration**: Register facilities and professionals
- Create Healthcare Professional ID (HPID) on the Healthcare Professionals Registry (HPR)
- Onboard facilities to the Health Facility Registry (HFR)
- Note: NHA reviews facility onboarding and can take days, so this should start early to avoid blocking go-live

Not all systems need all milestones—they depend on your role and use case. For example, a system that only creates records doesn't need M3.

The catalogue also references P1, P2, P3 phases which appear to be related to production or other gateways (UHI, NHCX).

Source: [ABDM Developer Portal Glossary](https://abdm-docs.eka.care)
